title: Change the conditions for a personal watercraft (PWC) driving licence
summary: PWC licence holders must visit a Service NSW Centre in person to change conditions on their licence, especially if there are changes to medical or physical conditions like eyesight.
intro:
As the holder of a PWC licence you'll need to notify Transport for NSW of any changes to medical/physical conditions, including eyesight, that might cast doubt on your fitness to operate a PWC.

To change the conditions on your PWC licence you can do so in person at a Service NSW Centre.

Note: Changes to eyesight conditions will require a replacement licence.
who_can_apply: Must be a current holder of a PWC licence.
Must be able to visit a Service NSW Centre in person.
what_you_need: A copy of your current Australian driver licence (to indicate eyesight conditions)
The completed 'Adjustment of Records – Maritime Customers Only' form
The 'Application for a Personal Watercraft Driving Licence' form
The 'Application for a Replacement Product' form
If adding or removing an eyesight condition, you may need to undergo an eyesight test at the service centre.

how_to_steps.text: Make sure you have all the required documentation.
Visit a service centre and provide the information in person.

faqs.q: What should I do if my medical or physical condition changes?
faqs.a: You must notify Transport for NSW of any changes to medical or physical conditions, including eyesight, that might affect your ability to operate a PWC.

faqs.q: How do I change the conditions on my PWC licence?
faqs.a: You must visit a Service NSW Centre in person to change the conditions on your PWC licence.

faqs.q: Do I need a replacement licence if my eyesight condition changes?
faqs.a: Yes, changes to eyesight conditions will require a replacement licence.
